compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Rebar resolves configuration through multiple authorities during one operation, and some backends reread ambient state after receiving explicit config. Authentication is also composed inconsistently across LLM, Git, bridge, MCP, review-bot, observability, and op-cert boundaries. This can change behavior mid-operation, discard an explicit choice, expose static credentials to unrelated children, or fall back through an unintended identity. RP-04 establishes one application-wide composition contract without making Rebar a credential store.

The approved research is on `relevant-liberal-xantus`; ADR 0098 is authoritative. Landed RP-01 (`08bcb1f9`–`f0275172`) is the LLM baseline RP-04 must extend.

## Approved design
- Resolve one immutable, serializable, non-secret `OperationSnapshot` at each operation boundary. Precedence is explicit operation input > environment > project config > user config > schema default.
- Resolve repository root separately: explicit `repo_root` > `REBAR_ROOT` > Git top-level/current directory. Interpret winning relative paths against that root.
- CLI composes once per invocation; MCP and Python once per operation; long-running processes also own startup deployment policy and live runtime bindings. An in-progress operation does not reread environment, files, cwd, or global config.
- Compose subsystem-local `GitRuntime`, `LLMRuntime`, and selected `BridgeRuntime` bindings. SDKs/helpers own credential issuance, storage, refresh, expiry, invalidation, and native precedence; Rebar-owned factories retain transport/output policy. `LLMRuntime` enters only RP-01's existing `PydanticAIRunner` -> per-run `ProviderSession` -> one-Agent path. Preserve its budget, complete-or-omit retry history, cache/accounting, typed exhaustion, artifacts, tracing, usage, and failure translation. No arbitrary client/runner injection or second scheduler/owner/path.
- Represent unavoidable static material with provider-specific, non-serializable Pydantic `SecretStr`/`SecretBytes` carriers, revealing it only in the sending adapter. Do not add a universal secret broker, central credential union, automatic keyring fallback, or application-owned cloud-secret retrieval.
- Trusted same-capability children inherit ambient environment for Git/SSH/AWS/proxy/CA compatibility. Rebar never installs credentials through global `os.environ` mutation. An owning child receives its adapter overlay; unrelated sibling children remove exact secret names declared by other Rebar adapters. Deployment/container/process boundaries remain the primary isolation mechanism.
- Static bindings rotate on restart/redeploy; SDK-native refresh remains SDK-owned.
- Op-cert accepts exactly one of `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` (preferred) or `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY`, validates before queue/worker/network/workspace creation, and copies the key into a process-owned 0700 directory/0600 file. Jobs receive context-local signer/principal/push-policy bindings. Remove runtime SSM/boto3/region coupling and per-job retrieval. Deployment may retain ADR 0049's SSM-at-rest source by injecting/mounting the resolved secret before process startup.
- Fail closed when explicit provider/profile/project/auth composition fails; never retry anonymously or as another ambient principal. Preserve optional write-only Langfuse/OTLP observability's fail-open/no-op behavior.
- Add a portable-local-and-CI AST ownership gate beside `check_config_reads.py`. It derives config/credential names from authoritative registries, rejects reads/reloads/defaults below approved seams, red-proves aliases/access shapes, permits only exact path/symbol+rationale exceptions, and reaches zero legacy exceptions at cutover.

## Scope
RP-04 only: central non-secret resolution/provenance, operation projections, runtime bindings, provider-native auth injection, static-secret handling, op-cert startup composition, all affected CLI/library/MCP/reconciler/hosted consumers, ownership gates, generated operator documentation, migration, and canaries. RP-02/RP-03 and RP-05/RP-06 remain separate.

Explicit corrections: CLI input outranks environment for `tracker.dir`; malformed config fails before effects; backends stop reloading; supplied Python config stays authoritative; defaults move to the schema; tracker layout reaches every owner; Jira Cloud write scope loses `DIG`. Other auth, redaction, retry, TLS, and output behavior changes require an explicit child decision and test.

## Migration / rollback
Expand in shadow mode, prove parity/deltas and non-leakage, cut consumers over behind compatibility facades, add gates/docs/canaries, then remove legacy paths. Before write cutover, disable shadow composition to roll back; afterward require the snapshot-aware compatibility floor. Stored ticket/bridge formats do not change, and parity diagnostics never persist credentials.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] CLI, MCP, Python, and direct reconciler paths produce equivalent non-secret behavior from the approved precedence/root contract; a captured operation is stable across environment/file/cwd mutation while the next operation observes the change.
- [x] Every affected consumer receives an immutable projection/runtime binding and no in-progress operation rereads ambient state.
- [x] A portable-local-and-CI AST ownership gate derives names from authoritative registries and rejects direct/aliased `load_config`, ambient config/credential reads, backend reloads, and configurable adapter defaults below approved seams; exact path/symbol+rationale exceptions contain no post-cutover legacy entry.
- [x] The LLM cutover injects provider-native auth/session capability only through the landed RP-01 `ProviderSession` builders; RP-01's one-run/one-Agent request budget, complete-or-omit retry history, cache/accounting, typed exhaustion, final artifacts, candidate tracing, usage, and failure behavior remain green in authoritative offline oracles and bounded live Anthropic/Bedrock cache/auth canaries.
- [x] Git and bridge factories preserve provider-native auth lifecycles and instantiate only the selected integration; missing/conflicting decision-bearing auth fails before network/write without anonymous, cross-provider, or alternate-principal fallback.
- [x] Secret canaries are absent from repr, equality/hash, serialization, snapshots, fingerprints, caches, provenance, exceptions, logs, output, argv, URL/query strings, subprocess siblings, and CLI/MCP schemas, verified at behavioral boundaries.
- [x] Same-capability children preserve unknown ambient/native-chain variables, owning children receive only their overlay, unrelated siblings lose exact Rebar-declared secret names, and concurrent operations observe no global environment mutation.
- [x] Op-cert enforces its exclusive startup sources, fails invalid composition before service work, uses a stable process-owned 0700/0600 copy and context-local signer, observes replacement only after restart, deletes only its copy, and has no application runtime SSM/boto3/region dependency.
- [x] Generated config/security/operator docs cover precedence, lifecycles, restart/redeploy rotation, provider ownership, observability's exception, subprocess limitations, and deliberate behavior deltas; drift checks detect schema/docs divergence.
- [x] Legacy ambient/per-job composition is removed only after focused suites and bounded live paths pass; rollback retains accurate non-secret diagnostics.
- [ ] [operator-attested] AWS review-bot and reconciler check/dry-run/bounded-live canaries pass after cutover without credential leakage or unauthorized fallback. Epic comments record run/change IDs, timestamps, selected provider/auth-source kind, retry counts, and redacted outcomes.
  provenance: environment=hosted-production; principal=review-bot-and-reconciler; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — live post-cutover canaries passed; no unauthorized fallback or leakage; redacted evidence in the epic comment.
